name: Cosmetics and beauty retail
shape_facts: Store type: neighbourhood cosmetics shop, mall store, online-only, or wholesale/beauty supply to salons.
Imported vs local brands, and whether they import directly or buy from distributors.
Number of SKUs and shades carried.
Channel mix: walk-in, Instagram/TikTok, own website, marketplaces (Daraz, Noon, Amazon).
Delivery method: own riders, courier, COD share.
Whether they also run beauty services (makeup artist, testers, consultations).
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems such as shade-level stock, expiry, tester wastage, online order flow, COD returns, influencer campaign tracking and staff selling. pi does not advise on product safety, ingredients, skin conditions, allergic reactions or which product suits someone’s skin. It does not advise on import licensing or cosmetic registration rules, or say whether a product is genuine. pi never records customer photos, skin details, phone numbers or addresses.

vocabulary.shade: colour variant of a product, each a separate SKU
vocabulary.RTO: return to origin, undelivered COD parcel
vocabulary.restock drop: announcement that a popular item is back

problems.phrase: Best-selling shades go out of stock and we only notice when customers ask
We have boxes of colours nobody buys
Products expire before we sell them
Testers get used up or stolen and we don’t count the cost
Small items walk out of the shop
COD orders get refused at the door and the courier charges us both ways
Courier COD money comes late and doesn’t match
Instagram DMs are full of ‘price?’ and ‘is this original?’ and we can’t reply to all
We pay influencers and don’t know what we got
Website stock and shop stock never match, so we oversell
Daraz/Noon listings show wrong stock or wrong price
Customers complain we sent the wrong shade
Imported shipments stuck at customs and we miss the season
Distributor raised prices and I didn’t update mine
Customers buy once in a sale and never come back
We don’t know who our customers are, everything is walk-in
Discount codes get shared everywhere and used too much
Sales girls don’t know the products, so they can’t recommend
Batch codes not tracked, so when a customer complains we can’t trace it
Bad reviews about late delivery are hurting the page
I don’t know my margin per product after courier and returns
White Friday / 11.11 orders crash our system
Staff do their own discount to friends

stock: How many products and shades do you roughly carry?
How do you find out something is running low?
expiry: Do expiry dates get checked, and by whom?
What happens to products close to expiry?
online orders: Where do most orders come from, Instagram, website, marketplace or walk-in?
How does an online order reach the person packing it?
cod and returns: How much of your online business is COD?
What happens when a parcel is refused?
marketing: Do you work with influencers or run ads?
How do you tell what each one brought in?
customers: Do you keep any record of who buys from you?
How do you let them know about new stock or a sale?
suppliers: Do you import directly or buy from distributors?
What usually goes wrong with deliveries?
staff: How many people sell in the shop?
How do they learn about new products?
loss: Are testers and small items counted at any point?
Where do you think most of the loss happens?
reporting: At the end of the month, how do you work out what you actually made?

seasons: In PK: Eid ul Fitr (Chaand Raat is huge), wedding season (October to March), White Friday / 11.11 / 12.12 on Daraz and brand sites, and summer for sunscreens. In the UAE: Ramadan and Eid, Dubai Shopping Festival, White Friday / Black Friday, Singles’ Day sales on Noon and Amazon, Diwali, and the slower summer months. In Canada: Black Friday and Boxing Day, Christmas gift sets, Valentine’s and Mother’s Day, and summer for sun care. Beauty also spikes around viral social trends that are hard to predict.
care: Never advise on ingredients, product safety, allergies, skin conditions or what to use. If someone describes a severe reaction (swelling, breathing difficulty), pi tells them to seek emergency care.
Never help sell counterfeit or “first copy” products as originals, repack or relabel expired stock, or change expiry dates.
Import permits and cosmetic registration are regulatory; pi notes only the operational effort or delay.
Do not record customer photos, skin information, phone numbers or addresses.
Influencer disputes: note the business issue, not the person’s name.
Refuse to help bypass customs or under-declare imports.
Staff theft suspicions are recorded by role and pattern only.
build_ideas: Shade-level stock with barcode scanning, reorder points and low-stock alerts on WhatsApp.
Expiry and batch tracker with near-expiry lists to plan bundles or clearance in time.
Tester log: opened, replaced, cost written off per month.
Unified stock across shop, website, Instagram and marketplaces to stop overselling.
Order desk pulling Instagram/WhatsApp, website and marketplace orders into one pick-pack list with shade check.
COD and courier reconciliation: dispatched, delivered, refused, remitted, outstanding.
Pre-dispatch confirmation message to COD buyers to reduce refusals.
Influencer and campaign tracker with unique codes and the sales they brought.
Customer list (with consent) and WhatsApp broadcast for restocks and sales.
Discount-code rules with usage caps and reports.
Product knowledge cards for staff on phone.
Margin per product after courier, returns and marketplace fees.
